documented: Gitleaks v8.30.1 supplies the candidate grouping alternatives, boundaries, uppercase-letter/digit alphabet and strict entropy threshold of 3.8.
The provider documents 34 alphanumeric characters: a two-character version, six-character public identifier and 26 secret characters.
The whitepaper states that hyphens are not part of the actual Secret Key; the native extension recognizes the unhyphenated representation.
The whitepaper describes a 31-character generation alphabet without enumerating it.
assumptions: Synthetic positives assert current detection behavior, not issuer-valid keys or a fully established generation alphabet.
The upstream candidate alphabet and entropy are a pinned matching baseline, not a provider-proven validity contract.
Only the upstream grouped presentations and the unhyphenated A3 representation are recognized; arbitrary separators and other versions are not inferred.
Provider acceptance of a presentation as authentication input is not established by recognizing its underlying key material.
Upstream example/value allowlists and inline gitleaks:allow directives are intentionally not imported.
evidence.fixture_method: Hand-constructed synthetic A3 candidates retain both original presentations; an upstream grouping alternative is added. Negatives distinguish missing material, unsupported versions/alphabet, unsupported separator placement and an upstream-entropy rejection. Every assertion describes the current detector contract, not issuer authenticity.

documented: Gitleaks v8.30.1 supplies the discovery prefix, encoded opening, minimum encoded length, Base64 candidate alphabet and strict entropy threshold of 4.
The provider explicitly documents the discovery prefix and Base64 URL encoding of a serialized SRPx object, with a decoded JSON-object example.
RFC 4648 specifies the standard and URL-safe Base64 alphabets and padding mechanics.
assumptions: Synthetic positives assert detection behavior, not valid issuance, authentication or a normative SRPx schema.
The provider does not establish required/optional SRPx fields, their exact alphabets or the relationships among cryptographic components; the previous example-derived field checks are removed.
The source also calls the representation a JWT, without reconciling that terminology with its single encoded JSON-object example; compact JWT semantics are not inferred.
The upstream minimum length, encoded opening and entropy remain baseline assumptions; arbitrary whitespace before the JSON opening and shorter objects are outside this rule.
JSON-object decoding and valid standard/URL-safe Base64 transport remain structural checks, not issuer validation; the 16 KiB candidate cap is local.
Upstream example/value allowlists and inline gitleaks:allow directives are intentionally not imported.
evidence.fixture_method: The original independently serialized synthetic JSON-object candidate is retained. Standard and URL-safe padded encodings of one derived synthetic object exercise transport only, without asserting its fields are issuer-valid. Original required-field, key-type and component-width negatives move to diagnostic because their expectations lacked a normative schema. Short candidates, incomplete padding and a sufficiently long malformed JSON object remain detection-contract negatives.

documented: X25519 identities contain exactly 32 secret bytes.
The generator emits uppercase AGE-SECRET-KEY- Bech32 identities; the parser requires that uppercase human-readable part.
Bech32 decoding checks the checksum, rejects mixed case and nonzero padding, and distinguishes the private identity from age1 public recipients.
assumptions: This source-backed native typed/carrier scope is retained independently of upstream rules; matching names do not imply equivalent detection or issuer authenticity.
evidence.fixture_method: A fixed synthetic 32-byte value is independently Bech32-serialized with the vendor human-readable part. Public recipients, checksum mutations, mixed case, truncation, excess data and noncanonical padding are separate negatives.

documented: age hybrid identities use uppercase AGE-SECRET-KEY-PQ- Bech32 encoding.
The pinned HPKE hybrid KEM generator and NewPrivateKey require a 32-byte seed.
The private-key parser preserves and checks the human-readable part, checksum, case and padding; age1pq public recipients are a different encoding.
assumptions: This source-backed native typed/carrier scope is retained independently of upstream rules; matching names do not imply equivalent detection or issuer authenticity.
evidence.fixture_method: The same independent fixed 32-byte seed is Bech32-serialized under the distinct PQ human-readable part and checksum. Public-recipient, wrong-checksum, padding, length and mixed-case specimens are negative.

documented: Bearer authorization is a credential carrier; compact JWS uses three dot-separated unpadded Base64url components.
The protected header and JWT claims are UTF-8 JSON objects.
JWA and EdDSA specifications define algorithm-specific MAC/signature encodings and widths; Ed25519 and Ed448 have fully specified JOSE identifiers.
assumptions: Only an explicit Bearer carrier is covered; bare JWT containers, form/query carriers, JWE, unsecured tokens and unknown algorithms are excluded.
The 16 KiB candidate and 8192-bit RSA-signature upper bounds are local limits.
Correctly sized signature bytes are not proof of signature validity, issuer, audience, expiry or authorization.
This source-backed native typed/carrier scope is retained independently of upstream rules; matching names do not imply equivalent detection or issuer authenticity.
evidence.fixture_method: Independent JSON and strict Base64url serialization with synthetic algorithm-sized signature bytes, not signatures copied from issued tokens. Negative records independently mutate JSON shape, header case, algorithm, signature width, padding, trailing components and canonical bits.

documented: PEM uses five-hyphen BEGIN/END boundaries, matching case-sensitive labels and Base64-encoded typed contents; RFC 7468 permits LF, CRLF and CR line endings.
OpenSSH private-key framing includes cipher/KDF declarations, matching check integers, typed private keys and numbered padding.
The pinned SSH parser and Go x509 parsers recognize supported unencrypted private-key containers.
assumptions: A header must start the value or follow LF; standalone CR-only armor is supported, not arbitrary CR-delimited surrounding text.
Selected unencrypted containers are covered, not encrypted keys, PGP or every accepted key representation.
The 16 KiB armor and 3072-bit legacy DSA bounds are local work limits.
Parsing a synthetic private key does not establish deployment, ownership or active use.
This source-backed native typed/carrier scope is retained independently of upstream rules; matching names do not imply equivalent detection or issuer authenticity.
evidence.fixture_method: Independently generated never-deployed RSA, EC, Ed25519, X25519 and DSA material serialized as DER/PEM and OpenSSH frames, with LF/CRLF/CR transport variants. Negatives mutate labels, DER, framing, seed/public consistency and padding, and distinguish public/encrypted containers.
